problem_text:
A municipality aims to formulate a coastal water-quality improvement strategy to lower total nitrogen runoff from several agricultural drainage outlets. Initially, no mitigation practices have been implemented.

The profile of each drainage outlet is as follows:
* For Outlet A, the nitrogen release coefficient is 2.786, and the associated cultivated area is 111.657 units.
* For Outlet B, the nitrogen release coefficient is 1.647, and the associated cultivated area is 190.342 units.
* For Outlet C, the nitrogen release coefficient is 1.162, and the associated cultivated area is 115.685 units.

To address the runoff, several best management practices (BMPs) are under consideration, each offering a specific nutrient removal rate:
* Implementing Practice X achieves a 43% reduction in nitrogen load.
* Implementing Practice Y achieves an 18% reduction in nitrogen load.
* Implementing Practice Z achieves a 58% reduction in nitrogen load.

Adopting a BMP at an outlet entails an additional cost per unit of cultivated area. The cost matrix for all outlet–BMP pairings is provided below:

| Outlet \ Practice | Practice X | Practice Y | Practice Z |
|-------------------|------------|------------|------------|
| Outlet A          | 51.671     | 199.532    | 106.81     |
| Outlet B          | 27.273     | 18.952     | 30.833     |
| Outlet C          | 129.215    | 160.495    | 90.21      |

The decision involves selecting which BMPs to apply to each drainage outlet (outlets may employ multiple practices concurrently), and it is permissible for an outlet to be only partially mitigated if required.
The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate nitrogen runoff is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.232 of the baseline load, while minimizing the total implementation expenditure.
